text:
deploy-bot: Release RC-2026-03-21 (build abc123) preflight finished. Vulnerability scan summary: 1 HIGH (CVE-2026-0001, libx), 3 MEDIUM, 5 LOW. SBOM uploaded to artifact-store. Security gate: manual approval required before full rollout.

maya: Pinging @omar for triage. If the HIGH is exploitable in our runtime we should consider rollback to previous image. Otherwise can we timebox a hold and patch?

omar: On it. Can you paste the scanner excerpt? also need reproduction steps.

deploy-bot: ````
VULN: CVE-2026-0001 libx <=1.2.3 - RCE?
Path: /app/vendor/libx
Evidence: sanitizer found suspicious input handling in parse_fields()
Exploitability: remote-untrusted input via websocket -> needs further confirmation
Severity: HIGH
````

jordan: If this is remotely exploitable in our websocket handler, we should pause canary immediately. Alternative: pin the canary fleet to `rel-2026-03-20-safe` (prev image) and continue limited validation. Pinging buys us time for a mitigation.

omar: Quick static grep shows usage of `parse_fields` in two spots: websocket handler and admin import. Repro attempt queued (running in vuln-lab). ETA ~45–90m.

lee: From Legal: any export/license flags tied to the lib? Also flagging potential customer notification requirements if we escalate to rollback. Please include a short impact blurb.

maya: Action proposal: 1) Pause full rollout, keep canary paused. 2) Pin canary instances to `rel-2026-03-20-safe` for 2 hours to avoid customer impact. 3) Security (omar) to confirm exploitability within 2 hours. 4) QA (qa-bot) to run the smoke/regression suite on pinned image. 5) Release notes freeze and prepare note template for customers if we need a rollback. Approve?

qa-bot: Smoke run on `rel-2026-03-20-safe` started. Initial status: all basic health checks OK. Running integration tests next (ETA 25m).

jordan: I can do the pin + resume canary traffic routing. Will coordinate with infra.

omar: Update: vuln-lab repro failed at first step; looks like exploit requires a specific header pattern we don't send by default. Still investigating but likelihood of widespread exploit appears low.

lee: OK — legal doesn't see a mandatory disclosure yet, but keep us looped. If we roll back, we'll need to publish a customer-facing note; I'll prep a draft.

maya: Decision: implement temporary pin to `rel-2026-03-20-safe`, pause the broader rollout, and timebox hold for 2 hours. If omar confirms exploitable path within that window -> full rollback and exec communications. If not exploitable, we will allow a gradual resume after patch/mitigation or acceptance signoff.

jordan: Pin applied to canary and throttled traffic restored at 5% for monitoring.

omar: Will post final exploitability verdict here in ~60m.

maya: Thanks everyone. Note: changing change window end by +2h to allow triage. I'll update the changelog and the release ticket. :white_check_mark:
